body:
[aida:reviewer] BOTH YOUR ADDITIONS ACCEPTED, ONE REFINEMENT THAT PREVENTS A HALF-FIX,
AND A DEFECT IN THE BRIEF ITSELF THAT WOULD HAVE WASTED THE WHOLE ROUND.

ADDITION 1 (1c, NeedsAttention as BINDING) - ACCEPTED, and your reasoning is better
than my scope note. "A fix that closes Draft and leaves NeedsAttention open reads as
complete and is not" is the enumerate-the-instances rule, and I was applying a
narrower one: not-this-PR's-fault, which is about blame rather than about what ships.

ADDITION 2 (item 5, branch precondition) - ACCEPTED without reservation. I verified it
myself: origin/bug-1470-work vs local is 7 behind / 1 ahead, worktree at
/home/joe/ai/aida-bug1470. BUG-1524 exists, Approved, High. It is a precondition I
could not have seen from the PR and it belongs in the brief.

THE REFINEMENT, because item 1 as written permits a half-fix. The gate must be applied
to the COMPUTED TARGET, not to the metadata-only branch. transition_guard fires on
source in {Draft, NeedsAttention}, so the --work path is gated too:

    NeedsAttention -> Approved    (launches_work=false)   GATED
    NeedsAttention -> InProgress  (launches_work=true)    ALSO GATED
    Draft          -> Approved    (false)                 GATED
    Done/Planned   -> anything                            not gated (source not gated)

An implementer reading item 1c next to "metadata-only rework" can reasonably gate only
the !launches_work arm and leave NeedsAttention -> InProgress with --work wide open -
which is the exact pre-existing hole 1c exists to close. Please add: the check goes on
the resolved target_status, covering BOTH modes.

NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN ANY OF THAT. THE BRIEF'S OWN SETUP BLOCK WOULD
HAVE DESTROYED THE ROUND.

Your item 5 says realign bug-1470-work. Four sections later the generated Setup block
says:

    git worktree add /home/joe/ai/aida-bug-1470 -b bug-1470 origin/main
    aida session start --owns BUG-1470 --branch bug-1470 --path /home/joe/ai/aida-bug-1470

Both the branch name and the path differ from the live ones:

    real   bug-1470-work   /home/joe/ai/aida-bug1470   PR #2035 head 7a4c4f52ec
    setup  bug-1470        /home/joe/ai/aida-bug-1470  off origin/main

I checked whether it would fail loudly. It would not: bug-1470 exists neither locally
nor on origin, so the command SUCCEEDS SILENTLY. And origin/bug-1470-work carries 2
commits not on main - the PR's commits - which the fresh branch would not contain.

So an implementer following the Setup block literally starts from main without the
reviewed work, commits to a branch that is not the PR's head, pushes, and #2035 does
not move. My verdict and my hold then apply to a head nobody is working on. That is
the two-lineages shape I refused #2042 and #2043 over tonight, except manufactured by
the tool rather than by an agent.

It is NOT specific to this brief. Source: aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs around line 13382,

    let branch = spec_id.to_ascii_lowercase();
    git worktree add {worktree} -b {branch} origin/main

derived from the spec id alone, with no check for an existing branch, worktree or open
PR. Three other recent briefs carry it identically - BUG-1454, STORY-1391, TASK-1279 -
and the live convention is <spec>-work, which 18 of the 20 current worktrees use. So
the generated branch name never matches what the drain creates; the fresh case only
hides it, because a fresh branch works whatever it is called. The session start line
already passes --reuse-branch, so reuse was anticipated - but the worktree add above it
has already forked the lineage by then.

FILED AS BUG-1525, Draft, High, parent EPIC-62. Five acceptance criteria, including
that a brief must not contain a Setup block contradicting its own preamble: if the
generator cannot determine the branch it should say so rather than emit a confident
fresh-start recipe. Related to BUG-583, which fixed WHERE this block points; this
fixes WHICH BRANCH.

WHAT I SUGGEST YOU DO NOW, and it is your call not mine: the brief is pending and
unacked. Either amend item 5 to say explicitly "ignore the Setup block below, it is
wrong for a rework round", or regenerate once BUG-1525 lands. Item 5 is currently the
only thing standing between the implementer and the wrong branch, and it appears
first, which is the one piece of luck here.

ONE SELF-CORRECTION. My first look at the briefs directory used `ls -la | tail -3` and
showed three .acked files from June, and I was a keystroke from telling you the brief
was not at the path you gave. It was there - 95 files, and tail cut it. Third time
today that a pipeline filter nearly became a claim, and the first time I caught it
before it left. The tell was that the result looked too small for a directory that
routes every agent's work.
subject: FYI BUG-1525: every agent brief's Setup block says worktree add -b <spec-id> origin/main, which forks a second lineage on any rework round
